primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL FEDERAL RESERVE HTML; table and explanatory text lines 252 and 271-272
primary_source_receipts.finding: In 2022, 54.3% of families held retirement accounts defined as IRAs, Keoghs and certain employer-sponsored accounts; conditional median $86,900 and mean $334,000. The 45.7% complement is lack of this account category, not proof of zero retirement-directed assets.

primary_source_receipts.claim: SHED adults with no retirement savings
primary_source_receipts.finding: About 28% of non-retired adults reported no retirement savings; 47% had retirement savings outside formal retirement accounts. Population and construct differ from SCF families/account ownership.

primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL VANGUARD PDF; PDF page 5 highlights, PDF pages 48-49 / Figure 51 and surrounding text
primary_source_receipts.finding: For Vanguard defined-contribution-plan participants in 2024, average balance $148,153 and median $38,176. Vanguard says current DC balances are only a partial preparedness measure and about 75% of participants were below the average.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Median household income available at publication
primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL U.S. CENSUS BUREAU 2024 INCOME REPORT; highlights line 178
primary_source_receipts.finding: 2024 median household income was $83,730; supports the script's rounded 'about $84,000'.

primary_source_receipts.claim: Personal saving rate available at publication
primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL BEA RELEASE ARCHIVE; April 2026 release lines 94-108; March 2026 lines 122-136
primary_source_receipts.finding: The latest release available before the 2026-06-09 upload reported April 2026 personal saving rate 2.6%; March was 3.6%. The script's 'right now about 3.5%' does not match the latest available month and may use an unstated older/revised value.

primary_source_receipts.access_scope: ORIGINAL NYU PROFESSOR DATA UPDATE; historical-context slide for 1928-2025
primary_source_receipts.finding: 1928-2025 U.S. stocks: 11.85% arithmetic average and 26 negative years out of 98. Supports broad average/negative-year framing; exact five-years-in-8%-to-12% count not independently reproduced here.

primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL SEC INVESTOR.GOV BULLETIN; lines 87-98 and 124-127
primary_source_receipts.finding: Ongoing fees reduce the balance earning returns; SEC's 20-year illustration shows materially lower terminal values as annual fees rise. The video's 'around a quarter' needs its own horizon/return assumptions.

primary_source_receipts.access_scope: OFFICIAL BLS CPI INFLATION CALCULATOR METHODOLOGY
primary_source_receipts.finding: Calculator uses calendar-year average CPI and latest monthly index for the current year. Script's 'mid-90s' and 'today' are insufficiently precise to reproduce exactly $211,000.

calculation_receipts.method: Independent Python calculations: end-of-month annuity with nominal annual rate divided monthly; annual compound-growth endpoints; contribution/return crossover; fee-drag endpoint ratios; frozen lifetime-rate peer medians
calculation_receipts.assumptions: No taxes or inflation unless noted; contributions at month end; nominal rates compounded monthly for contribution paths and annually for lump-sum examples; frozen views and age_days from VIDEO_MASTER.csv; first five peers are the PERFORMANCE_SENSITIVITY.csv cohort.
